findings.text: — §39 is declared `implementable` and its sibling §32 (same node shape, `reckon/ledger.py`) was wired into the plan with followup `f-tsigah-032` carrying `/reckon-build the-suite-is-green-at-head §32` (resolved 2026-10-21), while §39's addition in `393f3b01d` added no followup and the followup list still ends at the open `f-tsigah-038` for §38 — REASON: WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — the plan's own chain rule is that pending work is carried by an open followup with its one-line build invocation, and the plan is not closed, so as authored nothing in the chain names §39 as pending.

— the Deliverable says "Callers import from the new owner, which are `reckon/mcp.py` and `_build_roadmap`'s own call of `_dependency_endpoints`", but grep over the head tree shows `_qualified_plan` — a listed family member moved by this node — is called at `reckon/roadmap.py:824` and `:825` inside `_judgment_member` (`reckon/roadmap.py:808`), which is not in the moved family and stays in `reckon/roadmap.py`; the same Deliverable's "any helper only they call" phrasing is therefore also inconsistent with `_qualified_plan` being in the list — WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — the caller enumeration is stated as exhaustive and is the list the node imports against, so a node that trusts it while relocating `_qualified_plan` leaves `_judgment_member`'s two call sites unresolved; naming `_judgment_member` (or stating that `_qualified_plan` must be re-exported) is what makes the deliverable match the code it describes.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `every-plan-write-goes-through-edit-plan` §15 and `a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline` §50 both resolve to existing files carrying those ids, cited commits `cd279cc20` and `30f8a4198` resolve, all 21 `plan-commits` shas resolve, `docs/research/suite-failures-at-head.html` exists, and the cited line 2409 of `reckon/roadmap.py` is where the family begins.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §39's done-when is measurable (the width test passes at head, both modules' estimated tokens recorded) and names a declared negative control (restore `reckon/roadmap.py` to its base content in a scratch copy, and the width test names it again); that control is live because base content measures 51,232 tokens against the 50,000 bound, confirmed by running the test at head.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every log is required "under the run directory" under the coding and base arms, not a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new module is to be "named by what the family does"; no plan label, ticket number or version tag enters a symbol, filename or comment, and no ticket or changelog prose appears in the section.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §39's Deliverable states the moved names' callers exhaustively as `reckon/mcp.py` and `_build_roadmap`'s call of `_dependency_endpoints`, but `_qualified_plan`, itself a named member of the family, is also called from `reckon/roadmap.py` by `_judgment_member` at lines 824-825, a function that stays behind.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §39 carries one deliverable, moving the graph-target family out of `reckon/roadmap.py`, and one verdict closes it.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §39 is the only section in this plan that is declared `implementable` with no followup article added beside it, so the plan's followup chain still points only at §38.
